 The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 Criminal Petition No.5633 of 2020
Order:

entities.text: Baduru Sanju Sundhara Raj, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
-
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') to quash the proceedings in F.I.R. No.336 of 2020 dated 14.10.2020 of Gudur I Town Police Station, SPSR Nellore District registered for the offences punishable under Sections 272, 273,
328 and 188 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C.") and Section 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Gudur I Town Police Station, SPSR Nellore District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioners before this Court are A1 to A3 in the above said crime.

3. The case of the petitioners is that on 14.10.2020 at about 4:30 P.M. while the Police were performing patrolling duty near Aditya Provisional shop on the Eastern side of Old Bus Stand,
Gudur, petitioner No.1/A1 tried to escape on seeing the Police but the Police apprehended him.
On enquiry he revealed that himself and petitioner No.2 herein are purchasing prohibited gutka from petitioner No.3 to earn more money by selling the same.
Hence, the present crime is registered.

4. Heard Sri Raja Reddy Koneti, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that Sections 328, 272 and 273 I.P.C. and 59(i) of FSS Act relate to food safety standards.
Section 328 I.P.C. speaks about causing hurt by means of poison with an intention to commit an offence.
Section 272 I.P.C. speaks about adulteration of food or drink intended for sale and Section 273 of I.P.C. speaks about sale of Noxious Food or Drink.

He further submits that possession, sale, purchase and transport of banned gutka and tobacco products will not attract the offences as alleged as they do not fall under the definition of food and also do not spread any disease.
Moreover, the Police have no power to register the offences under above Sections except the designated officers like Food Safety Officer.
Further Section 188 I.P.C. would apply when there is disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant.
As such even Section 188 I.P.C. is not applicable to the present case.

6. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that in terms of the order passed in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, this Court has allowed several criminal petitions by quashing respective F.I.Rs.
Hence, he prays to allow this petition.

8. In the light of the above, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings in F.I.R.No.336 of 2020 dated 14.10.2020 of Gudur I Town Police Station, SPSR Nellore District, are hereby quashed against the petitioner herein.
